To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Central Asia is not a region, but a subsystem of Greater Central Asia, which in turn is a subsystem of Central Eurasia.
the United States is the most influential power in Central Asia and that Russia has the most potential to influence Central Asia in the long term.
Central Asia is not a core region of international relations, but that it is a core subsystem of the regional subsystems of Central Eurasia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the United States and Russia have structured Central Asia and with the consequences for the United States and for the world.
the structuration of international relations in Central Eurasia as they are played out in Greater Central Asia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the United States is a "great power" in Central Asia, but only in the context of a "great power game" in which it is the junior partner.
US-Russian strategic relations are the structuring force of international relations in Central Asia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the US-Russian competition for influence in Central Eurasia is the most important factor in the region's structuration.
the structuration of the Greater Central Asia region, and the Central Eurasia region in general, is a function of the strategic relations between the United States and Russia.
, in the first phase of the post-Soviet period, the United States was the dominant power in Greater Central Asia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the US-Russia relationship is the key factor that will determine how the region will develop in the coming decade.
the US-Russian competition in Central Asia has been structured by a series of strategic and operational imperatives.
, as a result of its own actions, the United States is now in a position of relative weakness in Central Eurasia, while the Russians are in a position of strength.
